question: Do same-scene human preference extremes identify one reusable source-free bounded global colour operator that moves held-out loser renders toward their preferred winner renders?

selection.label_semantics: pair label 1 means the right endpoint wins
selection.winner: unique maximum mean of 20 score columns
selection.loser: unique minimum mean of 20 score columns

acquisition.member_fetch: exact ZIP local-header plus compressed payload Range only

decode.integer_code_normalization: uint8/255 or uint16/65535 according to decoded sample depth

fit.operator: sigmoid(M logit(x) + b), one shared 3x3 M plus 3-vector b
fit.dose_selection: lowest fit target RMSE among candidates passing all analytic matrix gates; ties choose lower dose

controls: per-channel diagonal logit-affine at identical ridge and sampling
cyclically label-permuted winner targets at identical capacity
reverse-direction shared logit-affine applied in the forward direction

calibration_metrics.primary_error: mean OKLab Euclidean error to same-scene winner

stop_rules: Any parent, annotation, selection, byte-budget, Range, decode or role-leakage failure closes before fitting.
Any fit matrix gate failure closes without ridge, dose-grid or coordinate rescue.
Any calibration gate failure closes before sealed image acquisition.
No scene replacement, threshold relaxation, per-scene routing, higher-order operator or same-cohort rescue is allowed.
claim_ceiling: Private internal-research population-colour-prior D0 over same-scene ISP variants; not film, stock, scanner, calibrated authenticity, arbitrary-image preference, package, capability or product evidence.
